drills.coachNote: That bishop on e4 staring at h7 is the thing demanding your attention, not quiet development. drills.coachNote: Before recapturing, notice your bishop sits trapped on a1 with nothing defending it and Rf1 has the whole open first rank to reach it. drills.coachNote: Black's king has nowhere to go but e7 and f7 — your e3-e4 push is the one reserve tempo that can lock him in zugzwang, so the order you use it in matters. Playing Kf4 forced you to burn that e4 tempo right away (Kf7 e4 Ke7 Ke3), and you ended up back on e3 having already spent your only spare move, dropping from +19.8 to roughly +9. Kf3 reaches the same squares but saves a half-tempo through triangulation, so after Kf3 Kf7 e4 Ke7 Ke3 it's Black who runs out of useful king moves first. In king endings, count your spare tempo moves before you touch your king.

Ra7 blockades the a-pawn directly on its own file, where a rook in front of a passed pawn can't be dislodged without the enemy king walking the whole way around, buying your king time to help hold the draw. Rb2 makes that necessary move immediately, so when Black plays Bh3 you already have Rh2 ready to meet it, and your king is free to advance safely next (Ka3, Kc6). When a piece needs to move eventually, often it should move first, not last.

drills.title: vs koleapapa (479) — Indian Game
drills.coachNote: Black wants to throw in f4+ first — a free tempo check on your king on e3 — before dealing with the fact his c5 pawn is hanging and his rook on e8 is passive. Grabbing Qxc5 ignored that: Black gets f4+, you recapture gxf4, then b6 kicks your queen away, and you've spent moves untangling instead of finishing the game, turning a crushing +19.9 into merely a solid +7. Qf7 keeps the initiative instead, cutting off the king and working with your knight on e5 toward mate — Qf7 Rb8 Nd7 f4+ gxf4 g5 still wins material and keeps Black's king boxed in. When you're completely winning, favor the move that keeps generating threats over the one that just nets a pawn.
drills.threat: Black has f4+ in hand, a check that buys him time before his c5 pawn and boxed-in rook on e8 become real problems.

drills.explanation: Bd7 was the move — it keeps your pieces coordinated and avoids the tactic that punished your game move. In the game, Nh6 left that piece hanging: after Qxh6 it's simply lost.
drills.title: vs magdyis (520) — Grob Opening
drills.coachNote: White's queen has been eyeing that long diagonal the whole time, and once your g-pawn moved to g6 the h6 square lost its only natural defender — so Nh6 just hands the knight away for nothing, Qxh6 Bd7 Qg7 Rf8, a full piece dropped in a dead-even position. Bd7 develops safely instead, getting your bishop out and keeping c5 in reserve, and after Bd7 Rg3 c5 Qf4 Qc7 Qg5 the position stays balanced with all your pieces intact. Before you put a piece on a square, trace the diagonals and files that already point at it — don't just check if it's attacked now, check what's aiming at it.
drills.threat: Your pawn on g6 means nothing guards h6, and White's queen on c1 already sits on the c1-h6 diagonal.

drills.explanation: Qh4+ forks the king on e1 and the king on e1 — one of them falls next move. In the game, Rd2 ran into Nxe3, costing about 5.0 pawns of advantage.
drills.title: vs magdyis (520) — Grob Opening
drills.coachNote: White's plan is Nxe3, grabbing the advanced pawn that's been prying his king open and cooling your whole attack down — Rd2 gives White time for exactly that, and even though you answer with Rxg2 grabbing the queen, White just recaptures Nxg2, so you've traded your rook and attacking pawn for the queen instead of finishing the job outright, which is why the eval dropped from a crushing +12.4. Qh4+ keeps the pressure on immediately: Qh4+ Nf2 exf2+ Kf1 Rd1+ Ke2 drags the king into a mating net with every move forced. When you've got an attack rolling with a pawn this far advanced, keep throwing checks instead of repositioning pieces and giving the defender a chance to trade off your key attacker.
drills.threat: White's knight on d1 wants to jump to e3 and gobble the pawn that's been fueling your attack on his king.
